classification.difficultyReason: Model with three algebraic dimensions, expand to a cubic, find a root by trial, divide, reject the quadratic using the discriminant, and state the dimensions. Like backfill-9 with an extra expansion, about 48.

content.prompt: A rectangular box has width $x$ cm, a length that is 2 cm more than its width and a height that is 3 cm less than its width. The volume of the box is $70\text{ cm}^3$. Write a polynomial equation modelling this scenario and hence find the dimensions of the box.

answer.short: $x^3-x^2-6x-70=0$; the box is $7\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The width is $x$ cm, the length is $(x+2)$ cm and the height is $(x-3)$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+2)(x-3)&=70\\x(x^2-x-6)&=70\\x^3-x^2-6x-70&=0\end{align*}$$
Let $P(x)=x^3-x^2-6x-70$. Test factors of $70$:
$$P(5)=125-25-30-70=0.$$
Therefore $x-5$ is a factor. Long division gives
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+4x+14\\\hline x-5&x^3-x^2-6x-70\\&\underline{-(x^3-5x^2)}\\&4x^2-6x-70\\&\underline{-(4x^2-20x)}\\&14x-70\\&\underline{-(14x-70)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Hence
$$(x-5)(x^2+4x+14)=0.$$
The quadratic has discriminant $4^2-4(1)(14)=-40<0$, so its roots are not real. Hence $x=5$ cm, the length is $x+2=7$ cm and the height is $x-3=2$ cm. The box dimensions are $7\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$.
